questions.q: According to Anthropic's own current guidance, what is by far the most important factor in tool-calling performance?
options: Detailed, specific tool descriptions covering what, when, when-not, and each parameter
Using as few words as possible in the description
Always naming every tool 'tool_1', 'tool_2', etc.
Making every parameter optional
questions.explain: A brief, vague description leaves the model guessing; a detailed one (3-4+ sentences) gives it everything it needs to decide when and how to call the tool correctly.

questions.q: In the real get_stock_price example from Anthropic's docs, what did the 'good' description include that the 'poor' one didn't?
options: Nothing — both descriptions were functionally identical
A requirement that the ticker be a cryptocurrency symbol
What exchanges are valid, what currency is returned, when to use it, and what it explicitly does not provide
A list of every programming language the tool supports
questions.explain: The good version specified NYSE/NASDAQ validity, USD pricing, when to use it, and an explicit limitation — the poor version just said 'gets the stock price for a ticker.'

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend consolidating related operations like create_pr, review_pr, and merge_pr into one tool with an action parameter?
options: Because the Claude API only allows exactly one tool per request
Because fewer, more capable tools reduce selection ambiguity for the model
Because action parameters are required by JSON Schema
Because consolidation makes tool descriptions unnecessary
questions.explain: A larger set of near-duplicate tools increases the chance the model picks the wrong one; grouping related operations under one tool with a parameter narrows that ambiguity.

questions.q: What does 'meaningful namespacing' in tool names (e.g., github_list_prs, slack_send_message) accomplish?
options: It makes tool selection unambiguous as the tool library spans multiple services and grows larger
It is required for a tool's input_schema to be valid JSON
It automatically reduces the number of tokens a tool definition uses
It has no practical effect on model behavior
questions.explain: Prefixing names by service keeps tools from one system from being confused with similarly-named tools from another as the overall set grows.

questions.q: What does this lesson mean by designing a tool's response to return 'only high-signal information'?
options: Returning every field the underlying system has, just in case it's needed
Returning stable identifiers and only the fields Claude actually needs for its next step, not a bloated dump
Returning the response as an unstructured block of plain English prose only
Never returning any data at all, only a success/failure flag
questions.explain: A bloated tool result wastes context the same way a bloated prompt does, making it harder for the model to find and use what actually matters for its next decision.
